text:
The biggest story in Detroit is the player who isn't here. Dylan Larkin has refused to play until he is traded, and the Red Wings have suspended him. The reporting around it has turned to how far the two sides are apart; one widely circulated headline says Larkin believes his 10-team trade list is "enough." Until it resolves, Emmitt Finnie has his spot beside Lucas Raymond and Viktor Arvidsson, and Andrew Copp is playing more than 19 minutes a night.

The hockey itself has been strange. Detroit is winless in three and 1-4-0 in its last five, but our numbers have the Red Wings better than their record: 52% of the expected goals on the season and a -7 goal difference that should be about +3. Finishing has cost them roughly 11 goals. The other cost has been in net. John Gibson is at .860 and 6.3 goals worse than expected.

St. Louis is winless in three too, outscored 11-6, and the chances say that slide is real: 38% of the expected goals in those games. Joel Hofer has kept them close at .919 with 5.9 goals saved above expected. The Blues won the first meeting 5-4 on Oct. 31. Justin Faulk returns to St. Louis for the first time since leaving, after 482 games as a Blue, and Pius Suter is one goal from 100.

Our numbers call it a coin flip, 2.99 to 2.96. DeBrincat (35%), Arvidsson (34%) and Raymond (31%) are Detroit's likeliest scorers, all on the top power play. Our sleeper is St. Louis defenseman Philip Broberg, projected for nearly 27 minutes and 51% for a point.
headline: Red Wings without Larkin, still waiting on the finish

hunch.text: Eleven goals of bad finishing is a debt that gets paid somewhere. Our hunch is Detroit collects a little of it tonight against a team losing the chance battle.
